credits.name: OpenRA contributors
credits.role: Engine and upstream Red Alert 2 mod

set.whyWePickedIt: We'd pick this for the Red Alert 2 friend who wants another reason to argue about balance. Romanov's Vengeance takes that familiar battlefield and gives its developers room to change it. Bring a willingness to learn the differences, and treat the occasional rough edge as part of trying a work in progress.

faq.a: It builds on the OpenRA RA2 project, with its own multiplayer balancing and changes inspired by later Command & Conquer games. Expect differences from the original.
faq.q: Is this the original Red Alert 2 on a newer engine?

faq.a: The developers describe a custom campaign as planned, with little work completed. Choose this for its multiplayer focus rather than a finished campaign.
No. The project warns about bugs, missing original features, placeholder artwork and changing balance. Get your group onto the same release before arranging a match.

expected.whyWePickedIt: Red Alert 2 on a modern, supported engine.

set.whyWePickedIt: The appeal is seeing familiar C&C battlefields through OpenRA with the remastered artwork. We'd treat this as a side project for a curious fan who already owns the Remastered Collection. For a low-fuss game night, start with stock OpenRA; come here when experimenting with the presentation is part of the fun.

faq.a: Yes. Tiberian Dawn HD reads artwork from an existing digital installation of Command & Conquer Remastered Collection. Installing the engine alone does not provide those assets.
faq.q: Do I need to own another game?

faq.a: The project recommends a dedicated GPU but does not provide finalized requirements. Performance, memory use and loading times remain unoptimized, so we cannot promise that stock OpenRA requirements are sufficient.
We would start with stock OpenRA. Tiberian Dawn HD is explicitly a proof of concept; choose it when you want to experiment and can tolerate extra setup.
faq.q: Is this the recommended version for a first game night?

expected.whyWePickedIt: The original C&C in high definition.
